system_map.overview: The CAS runner orchestrates agentic workflows and automated architecture governance using declarative skill and subagent definitions, LiteLLM client abstraction, and telemetry adapters across coding agent runtimes.

agents.name: verifier
agents.role: Independent verification and architectural compliance audit of generated code and governance artifacts

agents.name: AgenticMerger
agents.role: Autonomous synthesis and conflict resolution of architecture decisions and governance branches

orchestration.description: FlowRunner coordinates pipeline execution, transitioning through GovernanceActionEngine and TransitionRegistry with deterministic validation before and after agent tasks.

patterns.name: Declarative Agent Skill Directory

tool_protocols.notes: Skills are exposed as modular command/prompt specifications in filesystem hierarchies.

optimisation_targets.notes: Decouples agent capabilities from agent host frameworks.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Allows agents to invoke discrete capabilities via version-controlled definitions.

patterns.summary: Agent capabilities and domain tasks are modularized as version-controlled directories of instructions, inputs, and schemas.
patterns.intent: Standardize how agent capabilities are defined, maintained, and shared across different agent runtimes.
patterns.context: Agent skills are partitioned under .agents/skills/ and mirrored for Claude under .claude/skills/.
forces: Cross-environment portability across different agent runners
Ensuring clear boundaries for agent tool invocation
patterns.solution: Organize each task into a folder with execution instructions, input parameter requirements, and schema validations.
implementation_signals: Separate skill manifests like cas-sync-archgov-reviews and cas-drawio-generator

evidence.note: Skill directory defining agent auditing rules
Skill directory defining architectural review synchronization

benefits: Zero code modification required to introduce or adjust agent capabilities
Discoverability and inspection of agent skill repertoires
costs: Risk of drift if skill manifests are replicated across multiple agent workspace configs
failure_modes: Stale prompt documentation leading to misaligned tool invocations

patterns.reuse_notes: Define agent capabilities in a runtime-agnostic folder pattern that syncs with environment-specific config files.

patterns.name: Subagent Verification Boundary

tool_protocols.notes: Verifier agent runs specialized verification passes.

optimisation_targets.notes: Prevents invalid architectural changes from reaching main branches.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Separates the primary generative actor from the validation actor.

patterns.summary: An isolated subagent performs read-only critical assessment and compliance verification on generated artifacts.
patterns.intent: Eliminate confirmation bias in primary agent generation by delegating validation to a specialized subagent.
patterns.context: Configured in .agents/subagents/verifier.md and .claude/agents/verifier.md to audit governance artifacts and PR changes.
forces: Generative agents tend to rationalize their own mistakes
Compliance checks require strict adherence to system constraints without context corruption
patterns.solution: Define an explicit subagent contract with strict inspection boundaries, dedicated instructions, and output formats.
implementation_signals: Dual role split between authoring agents and the verifier subagent

evidence.note: Mirror verifier agent declaration for Claude agent runtime

benefits: Objective evaluations unpolluted by generative working memory
costs: Increased LLM inference cost and latency during checks
failure_modes: Verifier agent accepting hallucinated evidence if checks are not backed by deterministic tools

patterns.reuse_notes: Implement independent verifier agent personas configured with negative testing checklists to audit outputs of primary agents.

patterns.name: Heterogeneous Agent Telemetry Adapter

tool_protocols.notes: Telemetry adapter reads and parses execution spans and trace events.

optimisation_targets.notes: Normalizes cost, token usage, and latency tracking across heterogeneous agents.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Transforms disparate vendor log/span formats into a uniform OpenTelemetry-aligned data model.

patterns.summary: Different agent runtimes (Antigravity, Claude Code, CodingAgent) have their proprietary spans ingested and transformed into a unified telemetry representation.
patterns.intent: Enable unified observability, cost tracking, and SLA auditing across differing coding agent platforms without locking into one runtime.
patterns.context: Implemented in src/cas_runner/dashboard/agent_telemetry.py with adapters for ClaudeCode and Antigravity.
forces: Agent vendors format logs and token counts inconsistently
Auditing enterprise AI usage requires unified cost and performance metrics
patterns.solution: Implement adapter classes extending a base telemetry parser that extract spans, calculate cost estimates in USD, and map into standard AgentTelemetrySpan instances.
implementation_signals: estimate_agent_cost_usd function with model pricing tables

evidence.note: Translates vendor-specific telemetry spans into normalized metrics

costs: Maintenance burden when vendor log formats or token schemas shift
failure_modes: Inaccurate USD estimates when newer models are introduced without updating the pricing lookup table

patterns.reuse_notes: Use this pattern when your team uses multiple AI coding assistants (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot) and needs uniform telemetry.

patterns.name: State-Transition Governance Engine

tool_protocols.notes: State transitions are managed through deterministic registry lookups.

optimisation_targets.notes: Constrains allowed agent operations according to strict lifecycle states.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: State changes are governed by rules rather than autonomous agent improvisation.

patterns.summary: Agent actions modifying governance artifacts are constrained by an explicit state transition registry that enforces allowed lifecycle transitions.
patterns.intent: Prevent agents from executing invalid or non-compliant mutations on architecture records.
patterns.context: Found in src/cas_runner/governance/governance_action_engine.py managing transitions across GovernanceAction lifecycle stages.
forces: Agents may skip mandatory review or compliance verification stages
State integrity must be maintained during automated architecture evolution
patterns.solution: Use a TransitionRegistry that explicitly checks whether a proposed state transition is valid before executing any governance action.
implementation_signals: TransitionRegistry class with explicit state transition lookups
GovernanceActionEngine evaluating actions against registered legal transitions

evidence.note: Registry and engine enforcing state transitions for governance records
Typed models representing actions and result transitions

benefits: Guaranteed consistency of artifact status transitions
Early termination of invalid agent action pipelines
costs: State registry must be updated whenever new workflow stages are introduced
failure_modes: Unhandled transition exceptions causing pipeline termination if fallback paths are omitted

patterns.reuse_notes: Wrap agentic state mutations behind an explicit finite state machine transition validator.

patterns.name: Agentic Artifact Merger

tool_protocols.notes: Uses LiteLLMClient to resolve conflicts between structured documents.

optimisation_targets.notes: Automates the reconciliation of conflicting architecture knowledge records.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: LLM reconciles differences while returning a structured ResolutionResult with traceable findings.

patterns.summary: Specialized agentic engine that reconciles conflicting decisions, narratives, and knowledge graphs into a coherent merged state.
patterns.intent: Resolve semantically complex merge conflicts in architectural decisions that rule-based 3-way git merges fail to handle.
patterns.context: AgenticMerger in src/cas_runner/governance/agentic_merger.py resolving governance and decision conflicts.
forces: Textual git conflicts in decision documents often require domain reasoning
Automated merging must not introduce architectural contradictions
patterns.solution: Pass conflicting revisions and contextual rule sets to an AgenticMerger that utilizes LLM reasoning to output a resolved artifact with detailed justification.
implementation_signals: ResolutionResult return models tracking resolution status and rationale

evidence.note: Agent implementation dedicated to merging architecture governance files
Typed model encapsulating merge outcomes and rationale

benefits: Semantic consistency across concurrent architectural updates
Reduction of manual triage for knowledge base synchronization
costs: Risk of subtle hallucinations or omissions in technical requirements
failure_modes: Failure to merge cleanly leading to unresolved conflict markers or degraded decisions

patterns.reuse_notes: Apply when structured domain records (ADRs, policies, models) must be merged across distributed branches.

patterns.name: Dual-Mode LLM Provider Abstraction

tool_protocols.notes: Standardized client interface supporting LiteLLM and deterministic mocks.

optimisation_targets.notes: Enables zero-cost offline regression tests alongside production model routing.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Isolates LLM invocation behind a unified interface allowing mocking in test suites.

patterns.summary: Unified LLM client abstraction providing seamless switching between production multi-provider routing (LiteLLM) and deterministic offline mocking.
patterns.intent: Allow end-to-end testing of agent workflows without requiring API keys, network calls, or incurring LLM costs.
patterns.context: Implemented in src/cas_runner/llm/ with LiteLLMClient and MockLLMClient sharing uniform call conventions.
forces: Testing agent pipelines requires deterministic, repeatable responses
Production workloads require resilient access to various LLM providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, HuggingFace)
patterns.solution: Define a unified client boundary where MockLLMClient can be injected into any agent component in place of LiteLLMClient.

evidence.note: Mock client for offline testing and deterministic CI runs

benefits: Zero token cost during continuous integration validation
Easy interception of generated prompts and responses for assertions
costs: Mock client must be maintained when prompt/response contracts evolve
failure_modes: Mock responses failing to reflect real-world LLM formatting quirks or truncation

patterns.reuse_notes: Always provide a pre-programmed mock client adhering to the exact production LLM client interface for test harness execution.

patterns.name: Workspace Agent Steering Injection

tool_protocols.notes: Injects governance and skill instructions into .claude/ and IDE configurations.

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures coding agents operate within explicit project governance rules.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Injects steering rules transparently into local workspace configs during bootstrap.

patterns.summary: Injects architecture governance rules, MCP settings, and subagent prompts directly into local IDE and coding agent configurations at workspace initialization.
patterns.intent: Ensure any AI assistant operating in the workspace automatically receives architectural guardrails and authorized skills.
patterns.context: Implemented in src/cas_runner/bootstrap.py via merge_cas_governance_block and merge_claude_settings.
forces: Developers run local coding agents without manual prompt preambles
Architecture rules must be enforced across all contributor sessions
patterns.solution: During workspace bootstrap, programmatically merge system governance blocks into project-level configuration files (.claude/settings.json, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md).

evidence.note: Merges governance blocks into Claude and agent configuration files

benefits: Consistent behavioral boundaries for all interactive agent sessions
Automated propagation of governance updates to developer workspaces
costs: Risk of overwriting custom user preferences in tool settings files
failure_modes: Malformed JSON during merge corrupting agent runtime settings

patterns.reuse_notes: Inject project governance instructions directly into the target assistant configuration files during repository bootstrap.

patterns.name: Schema-Grounded Compliance Engine

tool_protocols.notes: Applies programmatic and schema checks to agent-generated artifacts.

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures generated architecture artifacts strictly conform to system schemas.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Deterministic rule evaluation takes precedence over LLM discretion.

patterns.summary: Agent-generated decisions and models are evaluated against deterministic schemas and rules before being committed into the knowledge base.
patterns.intent: Prevent malformed or incomplete agent-authored architecture artifacts from polluting the persistent knowledge repository.
forces: LLMs can generate plausible yet structurally non-conforming YAML or JSON
Governance decisions need machine-verifiable compliance indicators
patterns.solution: Execute a dedicated ComplianceEngine pass that validates artifacts against schemas, returning structured ComplianceFinding records.
implementation_signals: ComplianceFinding and ComplianceMetrics models in models.py

benefits: Zero tolerance for schema violations in persistent records
Deterministic validation reports that can be directly passed back to agents for self-correction
costs: Schema changes require updating compliance definitions
failure_modes: False positives if schemas are overly restrictive regarding optional fields

patterns.reuse_notes: Couple agent generators with deterministic schema validators that output structured error findings to feed back into self-healing loops.

anti_patterns.name: Shadow Agent Configuration Divergence
symptoms: Skills and agent definitions are duplicated between .agents/ and .claude/ directory trees
Changes applied to one agent manifest may not be reflected in the parallel directory

where_observed.note: Agent skill definition in primary agents tree
Duplicated skill definition in Claude-specific tree

impact: Agent behavior diverges depending on whether run via CLI, Claude Code, or IDE plugins
Increased maintenance overhead and potential silent failures during execution
suggested_remediation: Maintain a single canonical source of truth for agent skills and symlink or project them during build/bootstrap via automated scripts.
Add CI validation to verify exact equality between mirrored skill directories.

anti_patterns.name: Static Rate Telemetry Cost Fallbacks
symptoms: estimate_agent_cost_usd falls back to hardcoded pricing heuristics or default rates when model IDs do not match the static lookup dictionary

where_observed.note: Static dictionary lookup for provider pricing

impact: Misreported governance and operational spend in dashboard analytics as provider pricing evolves or new models are queried
suggested_remediation: Delegate pricing calculations to LiteLLM's dynamic cost calculation utilities or dynamic upstream provider price feeds.
Record raw prompt and completion token counts distinctly from dollar estimates.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Integrated OpenTelemetry spans adapted from disparate agent runtimes and mapped to unified dashboards with cost and health scoring
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Essential for supervising multi-developer, multi-agent AI code generation.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Standardized markdown templates in cas-knowledge/templates/ providing structural schemas for ADRs, pattern proposals, and rule definitions
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Enforces uniform input/output schemas when agents generate or modify architecture artifacts.
